problem_statement: ICMP response handlers are dispatched purely by ICMP type and code, without regard to the packet's address family. As a result a malformed IPv4 packet that happens to carry an ICMPv6 message code is delivered to handlers registered for ICMPv6, and vice versa: an IPv6 packet carrying an IPv4 ICMP code reaches IPv4 handlers. A handler registered for one address family must only be invoked for packets of that same address family, so a malformed cross-family packet must not trigger a handler expecting the other family.

problem_statement_fixed: ICMP response handlers are dispatched purely by ICMP type and code, without regard to the packet's address family. As a result a malformed IPv4 packet that happens to carry an ICMPv6 message code is delivered to handlers registered for ICMPv6, and vice versa: an IPv6 packet carrying an IPv4 ICMP code reaches IPv4 handlers. A handler registered for one address family must only be invoked for packets of that same address family, so a malformed cross-family packet must not trigger a handler expecting the other family.
